newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Clear sues Telecom and NZ government.
newsitem.headline: Clear sues Telecom and NZ government.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 17 - Clear Communications said on Thursday it is suing Telecom Corp and the New Zealand government for what it calls breaches of undertakings.
Clear said it entered the market on undertakings by Telecom to the government in 1988.

"Telecom gave undertakings to government in preparation for deregulation that interconnection charges would be fair, consistent, non-discriminatory and based upon cost, and that it would separate national transmission facilities so as to ensure transparency," Clear said in a statement.
"These undertakings were publicly and formally announced by the government and the circumstances make it plain that the government intended that potential new entrants would rely upon them."
Clear alleges Telecom dishonoured the undertakings, resulting in large losses to Clear. Claims were also made against the government on the basis that it failed to ensure Telecom met its commitments.
